note: Sealed id crosswalk. A tcgPlayerId is written only when a hard id confirms the product. Name overlap was not used. None of the 207 products cleared that bar, so every tcgPlayerId stays null.
source: TCGCSV category 3 groups and product files, plus pokemontcg.io /v2/sets ptcgoCode.
whyNone: Product objects from https://tcgcsv.com/tcgplayer/3/{groupId}/products have no productType field. Keys are productId, name, cleanName, imageUrl, categoryId, groupId, url, modifiedOn, imageCount, presaleInfo, extendedData.

extendedData on the files that were opened is a key-value list. Names seen: Rarity, Number, Card Type, HP, Stage, Attack 1, Attack 2, Weakness, RetreatCost, Resistance, CardText, UPC. TCGCSV docs say Rarity or Number means the product is a card. That distinguishes a card from a non-card. It does not say ETB, booster box, bundle, pack, tin, or UPC.
The subtype stored on our sealed products is our own label. The subtype on data/catalog/tcgcsv-latest.json is parsed from the product name. Neither was treated as a product type field.
No sealed product stores a UPC or any other TCGplayer product id (no 12 to 14 digit token in the record). A UPC on the TCGCSV side cannot be checked against our id.

Where a groupId was found, it identifies the set only. Several non-card products sit in each of those groups, and the same UPC is reused across art variants, so the group id alone does not pick one productId.

placeholder.whatWasHashed: CDN files at https://tcgplayer-cdn.tcgplayer.com/product/{id}_in_400x400.jpg. imageCount 0 returns HTTP 403 with an XML body, sha256 a824bc7739e226e1b40ea0f8c4e4f4c6f796fc3b4abfa6e9abe3bd119a30d938, which is not a JPEG and does not start with 23c8d781. The 78 pattern jpegs that returned 200 are unique and none start with 23c8d781.
placeholder.whyZero: No sealed product received a tcgPlayerId, so none can be a confirmed id whose photo is the placeholder.

White Flare.groupJoin: abbreviation equals the only ptcgoCode (WHT or BLK)

Black Bolt.groupJoin: abbreviation equals the only ptcgoCode (WHT or BLK)

official.catalogue: data/card-catalogue.json has 173 rsv10pt5 cards and 172 zsv10pt5 cards from pokemontcg.io. None of those ids is a ball-pattern variant. The only name containing ball is zsv10pt5-79 Air Balloon, which is a card name, not a pattern.
official.imageByCardId: https://images.pokemontcg.io/rsv10pt5/1_hires.png is card id rsv10pt5-1 (Sewaddle, number 1). sha256 4f91ee0139826970bb704e297fffa86127ea5ae9aa7577c3e5e90220f6b41c3a. The same bytes are at https://images.scrydex.com/pokemon/rsv10pt5-1/large. The picture is the standard Sewaddle, not a Poke Ball or Master Ball pattern.
official.whyNotThePattern: TCGCSV lists separate products for the base card and each pattern, and they share a collector number. Sewaddle base product 642116, Master Ball 642290, and Poke Ball 642362 are all Number 001/086. The official card id follows that number. It is not the pattern productId. There is no second official id for the pattern.
